prompt.en: Why do people's wants keep changing over time? How does this affect production in an economy? Why can all our wants never be satisfied? (3 marks)

label.en: Explains that satisfying one want creates the next one, while new products, changing tastes and rising incomes keep the list moving

level1.en: Think about the week after a new game or gadget arrives — how soon do you start wanting the next one?

clue.en: Meera's basic phone led to a smartphone, then to wanting a bigger screen. Shops also keep selling things that did not exist last year.

level2Template.en: Wants change because the satisfaction of one want gives rise to ___, while new products and changing fashions create fresh desires.

label.en: Shows that producers respond to shifting wants by changing what they make — new goods get produced, fading ones are cut back

level1.en: When everyone suddenly wants the newest thing, what happens to the factories still making last year's model?

clue.en: Producers chase demand: a product nobody wants any more stops being made, while the new favourite gets fresh production lines.

level2Template.en: Producers respond to changing wants by adjusting ___, directing resources towards goods and services for which demand is rising.

label.en: Concludes that all wants can never be satisfied because resources stay limited while wants multiply without end

level1.en: If money, land and workers were endless, would anything be missing? So where does the real limit lie?

clue.en: The wish-list grows without end, but money, land, workers, machines and time stay limited — Meera's ₹500 never stretches to her ₹750 list.

level2Template.en: All wants cannot be satisfied because resources are ___ while wants are unlimited.

text.en: Human wants are unlimited and keep changing over time, and this shapes production in every economy.
